# Setup {#sec-setup .unnumbered}

Complete this before Week 1. Budget an hour; package installation is slow, especially on Windows.

## Hardware

A laptop with 16 GB RAM handles a 10k-cell PBMC dataset comfortably in either language. 8 GB works with care (close other applications; avoid the full Azimuth reference). Week 6 multi-sample analysis with 50k+ cells benefits from 32 GB.

## Choose a language

You need only one. Both are fully supported in every chapter.

- **R / Seurat** is the more common choice in immunology labs and has the richer plotting ecosystem for publication figures.
- **Python / Scanpy** scales better to very large datasets, integrates with deep-learning tools (scVI), and scirpy's TCR handling is rigorous.

## Get the course folder

All code in this course uses paths like `data/raw/filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5` and `data/processed/01_pbmc_qc.rds`. Those paths are **relative to the course folder**, which you download from GitHub. You do not create or name any folders yourself.

1. Go to <https://github.com/aezamora14/scRNA-immunology-course>.
2. Click the green **Code** button, then **Download ZIP**. (If you use git: `git clone https://github.com/aezamora14/scRNA-immunology-course.git` does the same.)
3. Unzip it somewhere you will keep for six weeks, e.g. `Documents/scRNA-immunology-course/`. Inside you will find:

```
scRNA-immunology-course/
├── chapters/          the six weekly sessions (the same text as this website)
├── data/
│   ├── raw/           ← put downloaded 10x files here
│   └── processed/     ← the code saves intermediate objects here
├── images/
├── install.R
├── environment.yml
└── scRNA-immunology-course.Rproj
```

`data/raw/` and `data/processed/` already exist (they contain only a hidden placeholder file). Everything you download goes into `data/raw/`; everything the code saves goes into `data/processed/`. Both folders are ignored by git, so if you later push your own copy to GitHub the large data files will not be uploaded.

::: {.callout-important}
## Your working directory must be the course folder
Relative paths only work if R or Python is running *from* the course folder.

- **RStudio:** double-click `scRNA-immunology-course.Rproj`. RStudio opens with the working directory set correctly; check with `getwd()`.
- **JupyterLab / VS Code:** open a terminal, `cd` into the course folder, then launch `jupyter lab` (or open the folder in VS Code). Check with `import os; os.getcwd()`.

If you see `FileNotFoundError` or `cannot open file 'data/raw/...'`, the working directory is wrong: nine times out of ten the fix is opening the `.Rproj` or `cd`-ing into the folder first.
:::

## Install: R

Install R ≥ 4.3 from <https://cran.r-project.org> and RStudio from <https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/>. Then, in R, run the course installer (the file `install.R` in the repository):

```r
source("install.R")
```

It installs Seurat v5, scRepertoire v2, scDblFinder, harmony, presto, clustree, speckle, edgeR and Azimuth. On macOS you may need Xcode command-line tools (`xcode-select --install`); on Windows, Rtools matching your R version.

Verify:

```r
library(Seurat); library(scRepertoire)
packageVersion("Seurat")        # should be >= 5.0
packageVersion("scRepertoire")  # should be >= 2.0
```

Leiden clustering (`algorithm = 4`) needs the Python `leidenalg` package reachable via `reticulate`. If that fails, use Louvain (`algorithm = 1`); the course content is unaffected.

## Install: Python

Install Miniforge or Miniconda, then create the course environment from `environment.yml` in the repository:

```bash
conda env create -f environment.yml
conda activate scimmuno
python -c "import scanpy, scirpy; print(scanpy.__version__, scirpy.__version__)"
```

Launch JupyterLab with `jupyter lab`. If you prefer VS Code, select the `scimmuno` interpreter.

## Download the data

The course uses a 10x Genomics **5′ Immune Profiling** human PBMC dataset with paired gene expression and TCR V(D)J libraries. Any such dataset from the 10x public data portal works:

1. Go to <https://www.10xgenomics.com/datasets> and filter by *Chromium Single Cell Immune Profiling*, species *Human*, sample type *PBMC*.
2. Choose a dataset that lists both a **Gene Expression** and a **V(D)J T** library from the same cells (datasets processed with `cellranger multi` are ideal).
3. Download the following files and move them into the `data/raw/` folder inside the course folder you unzipped above:
   - `filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5` (gene expression)
   - `raw_feature_bc_matrix.h5` (optional; for ambient-RNA correction)
   - `filtered_contig_annotations.csv` (TCR contigs)
   - The dataset's summary HTML, which reports how many cells Cell Ranger called

::: {.callout-warning}
If the GEX and V(D)J files come from separate Cell Ranger runs rather than one `multi` run, confirm that the barcode suffixes match (`AAACCTGAGAAACCAT-1` in both). Barcode mismatch is the most common Week 5 error.
:::

For Week 2's optional cell-cycle scoring in Python, also download `regev_lab_cell_cycle_genes.txt` from <https://github.com/scverse/scanpy_usage/tree/master/180209_cell_cycle> into the same `data/raw/` folder.

For Week 5's database queries, download the latest VDJdb export from <https://vdjdb.cdr3.net> (the `vdjdb.slim.txt` file) into `data/raw/` as well.

## Multi-sample datasets for Week 6 and the capstone

Suitable public datasets with paired scRNA + scTCR across several samples and a condition contrast include:

- Multiple healthy-donor 5′ PBMC runs from the 10x portal (null contrast; good for practising mechanics)
- Peripheral blood from COVID-19 patients versus healthy donors with V(D)J (several 2020–2021 studies deposited paired data in GEO; search GEO for "5' scRNA TCR PBMC COVID")
- Tumour-infiltrating T cells with matched blood (search GEO for "scTCR-seq tumor blood paired"; several melanoma, lung and colorectal studies deposited both libraries)

Check that the deposit includes per-sample `filtered_contig_annotations.csv` files, not just processed clonotype tables, or you will not be able to redefine clonotypes.

::: {.callout-note}
The instructor may replace these with a lab dataset. Substitution is seamless as long as the file names and layout under `data/raw/` follow the pattern above.
:::

## Verify your setup

Open R (via the `.Rproj`) or Python (launched from the course folder) and run the block for your language. The first line checks the working directory; if it does not end in `scRNA-immunology-course`, stop and fix that before anything else.


::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R (Seurat)
```r
basename(getwd())          # should print "scRNA-immunology-course"
list.files("data/raw")     # should list the files you downloaded
library(Seurat)
x <- Read10X_h5("data/raw/filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5")
if (is.list(x)) x <- x[["Gene Expression"]]
dim(x)   # roughly 36000 x (number of cells)
tcr <- read.csv("data/raw/filtered_contig_annotations.csv")
mean(sub("-\\d+$", "", tcr$barcode) %in% sub("-\\d+$", "", colnames(x)))  # should be ~1
```

## Python (Scanpy)
```python
import os; print(os.path.basename(os.getcwd()))   # should print "scRNA-immunology-course"
print(os.listdir("data/raw"))                       # should list the files you downloaded
import scanpy as sc, pandas as pd
a = sc.read_10x_h5("data/raw/filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5")
print(a.shape)   # (number of cells, roughly 36000)
tcr = pd.read_csv("data/raw/filtered_contig_annotations.csv")
print(tcr["barcode"].str.replace(r"-\d+$", "", regex=True).isin(
      a.obs_names.str.replace(r"-\d+$", "", regex=True)).mean())   # should be ~1
```
:::

If both print sensible values, you are ready.
